questions.question: Name the Allied Powers and explain how the alliance grew during the war.
questions.expected_answer: The main Allies in 1914 were France, Russia and Britain with its empire, including Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and India, together with Serbia, Belgium and Montenegro; France also used its empire. Japan joined in 1914, Italy in 1915 after the Treaty of London promised it territory, Romania and Portugal in 1916, Greece in 1917, and the United States declared war in April 1917 because of unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram. Russia left after its revolutions with the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in March 1918.

questions.question: Name the Central Powers and describe their strengths and weaknesses.
questions.expected_answer: The Central Powers, in the centre of Europe, were Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire, which joined at the end of October and beginning of November 1914, and Bulgaria, which joined in October 1915. Strengths: Germany's efficient army and industry, and interior railway lines to move troops between fronts. Weaknesses: being surrounded and fighting on several fronts, Austria-Hungary's losses and disloyal nationalities, the British naval blockade causing food shortages, and smaller resources than the Allies, especially after the United States joined. They collapsed between September and 11 November 1918.

questions.question: Explain why the conflict became a world war and describe South Africa's role.
questions.expected_answer: The war spread through several fronts: the Western Front from Belgium to Switzerland, the Eastern Front, the Italian and Balkan Fronts, Gallipoli, the Middle East and the sea, and through empires that brought in colonies and dominions. In Africa, Togoland and Kamerun were taken, South Africa under Botha and Smuts put down the 1914 Afrikaner rebellion and conquered German South West Africa by July 1915, and South Africans fought in German East Africa against Lettow-Vorbeck, who surrendered only after the armistice. South Africans also served in Europe and the Middle East, with black South Africans in the unarmed Native Labour Contingent.
